run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Social Network
Namespace: social-network

A social network with unidirectional follow relationships, implemented with loosely-coupled microservices, communicating with each other via Thrift RPCs.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The front-end API gateway of the social-network app, Deployment nginx-thrift (pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-r7jlt, namespace social-network), is in a crash loop: its container has 4 restarts, exit code 137, and is currently CrashLoopBackOff/not ready; an earlier snapshot of the same pod shows two terminations with reason OOMKilled (12:20:13Z and 12:20:34Z). The pod's container memory limit/request is 16Mi even though its owning Deployment nginx-thrift and ReplicaSet nginx-thrift-65f656c999 template declares limits memory 256Mi / requests memory 128Mi. The 16Mi value is exactly the hard-coded MEMORY = "16Mi" in the admission-webhook code stored in ConfigMap platform-policy-controller-server (namespace platform-ops), which JSON-patches container[0] resources.requests.memory and resources.limits.memory on pod CREATE. Five MutatingWebhookConfigurations were created at 2026-11-21T12:19:56Z pointing at service platform-ops/platform-policy-controller path /mutate with a namespaceSelector for social-network; the one that matches pods with no label gating (gatekeeper-mutating-webhook-configuration, pods CREATE, objectSelector {}) applies to this pod. The nginx-thrift pod was created at 12:20:04Z, after those webhooks existed, and it is the only one of the 27 social-network pods created after 12:19:56Z and the only one carrying any memory limit; all other pods were created 12:19:19-12:19:23Z and have no limits. The Deployment itself was rolled to a new ReplicaSet at ~12:19:50Z (old ReplicaSet nginx-thrift-68bc7d94df, which had no resource settings, was scaled down at 12:19:54Z), which is the restart mechanism that put a new pod in front of the webhook. The remaining 26 social-network pods are ready with 0 restarts; media-frontend, user-memcached and user-timeline-redis showed 0 available endpoints at 12:20:15Z but are now ready with 0 restarts after image pulls, so that was startup, not failure. The mutation itself was not observed in an admission log, and no change-history integration is available, so the conclusion is partial.

claims.text: Pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-r7jlt (namespace social-network) has container nginx-thrift with restartCount 4, ready=false, waiting reason CrashLoopBackOff, lastState.terminated.reason Error and exitCode 137.

An earlier snapshot of the same pod showed lastState.terminated.reason OOMKilled with exitCode 137 finished at 2026-11-21T12:20:34Z, and a BackOff event 'Back-off restarting failed container nginx-thrift in pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-r7jlt' was recorded at 2026-11-21T12:20:16Z.

The running pod's container nginx-thrift is configured with resources.limits.memory=16Mi and resources.requests.memory=16Mi (no probes), while Deployment nginx-thrift (generation 2) and ReplicaSet nginx-thrift-65f656c999 templates declare limits memory 256Mi and requests memory 128Mi.

ConfigMap platform-policy-controller-server in namespace platform-ops contains server.py with 'MEMORY = "16Mi"' and a build_patch() function that emits JSON Patch ops setting /spec/containers/0/resources/requests/memory and /spec/containers/0/resources/limits/memory to that value on every AdmissionReview it answers.

Five MutatingWebhookConfigurations were all created at 2026-11-21T12:19:56Z and point to clientConfig.service platform-ops/platform-policy-controller path /mutate, including gatekeeper-mutating-webhook-configuration (webhook mutation.gatekeeper.sh, apiGroups [""], resources ["pods"], operations ["CREATE"], namespaceSelector kubernetes.io/metadata.name=social-network, objectSelector {}).

The backing webhook process is Deployment platform-policy-controller (namespace platform-ops, container 'webhook', command python /app/server.py); its pod platform-policy-controller-7d44bbdc6b-mk7th was created 2026-11-21T12:19:54Z, is Running and ready, and mounts ConfigMap platform-policy-controller-server at /app.

Pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-r7jlt was created at 2026-11-21T12:20:04Z, after the webhooks were created at 12:19:56Z; the other 26 pods in social-network were created between 12:19:19Z and 12:19:23Z, and none of them has any memory limit set while nginx-thrift is the only pod with limits (16Mi).

Deployment nginx-thrift was rolled during the window: new ReplicaSet nginx-thrift-65f656c999 was created 2026-11-21T12:19:50Z with template memory 256Mi/128Mi, the previous ReplicaSet nginx-thrift-68bc7d94df (template resources {}) was scaled down from 1 to 0 at 2026-11-21T12:19:54Z and its pod nginx-thrift-68bc7d94df-kk8p6 was deleted, and the old pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-kktc7 was stopped at 12:20:04Z.

kube_endpoint_address_available{namespace="social-network",endpoint="nginx-thrift"} was 0 at every 15s sample from 12:19:30Z to 12:20:15Z, while 22 other social-network endpoints reported 1 at 12:20:15Z (media-frontend, user-memcached and user-timeline-redis also reported 0 at that instant).
The only pod in social-network not ready at 12:22:34Z was nginx-thrift-65f656c999-r7jlt (waiting CrashLoopBackOff); all other 26 pods were Running with ready containers and 0 restarts.

Sampled traces of service nginx-web-server for /wrk2-api/post/compose between 12:20:00Z and 12:20:15Z carry http.status_code=200 and show the full downstream fan-out (compose-post-service, text-service, url-shorten-service, user-mention-service, post-storage-service, social-graph-service, user-timeline-service, home-timeline-service, unique-id-service, user-service, media-service) completing in milliseconds.

media-frontend-864dc9bb45-crznt, user-memcached-554fcf9578-mgfz9 and user-timeline-redis-cbd5f6645-4rcc7 were the three other endpoints at 0 available addresses at 12:20:15Z, but each is now ready with 0 restarts, and their pods logged image pulls at 12:19:22-12:19:24Z; their momentary 0 is startup image pull and not a failure tied to this cause.

Rejected: the 256Mi limit declared in the nginx-thrift Deployment/ReplicaSet template caused the OOM. The container actually ran with a 16Mi limit, while both the Deployment (256Mi/128Mi) and ReplicaSet nginx-thrift-65f656c999 (256Mi/128Mi) templates declare 256Mi, so the crash cannot be explained by the 256Mi template value.

Rejected: nginx-thrift's failure is merely a startup readiness miss of a young pod. The container has terminated (OOMKilled/exit 137) repeatedly, has restartCount 4 and is in CrashLoopBackOff, and the pod declares no readiness or liveness probe, so this is a crash loop rather than a probe-timing artifact.

plausible mechanism: while the mutating webhooks created at 12:19:56Z remain registered against platform-ops/platform-policy-controller, every newly created pod in namespace social-network will have container[0] memory requests/limits forced to 16Mi by that admission patch, so any later restart or rollout of a social-network workload (not only nginx-thrift) would be capped at 16Mi and risk OOMKilled crash loops; only nginx-thrift has been observed to be created since the webhooks existed.

gaps: The admission request/response that stamped 16Mi onto pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-r7jlt was not captured: platform-policy-controller suppresses request logging (log_message returns) and no admission audit logs were available, so the mutation is inferred from the pod limit exactly matching the webhook's hardcoded MEMORY value and differing from the 256Mi ReplicaSet template.

No change-history integration is available, so it is unknown which actor updated Deployment nginx-thrift to generation 2 (adding limits 256Mi / requests 128Mi and creating ReplicaSet nginx-thrift-65f656c999 at 12:19:50Z) or which actor created the five MutatingWebhookConfigurations and the platform-policy-controller workload in platform-ops at 12:19:54-12:19:56Z.

fetch_pod_logs for nginx-thrift-65f656c999-r7jlt returned 0 lines for both the current and the previous container instance, so there is no application log evidence of the OOM (the pod's stdout/stderr appear empty); the OOM evidence is pod status plus events only.

Prometheus metric traces_span_metrics_calls_total had no series in the queried windows (no_data), so no aggregate request-error rate or latency series could be computed for nginx-thrift or any other service; the traces_search tool returned INVALID_PARAMS for every call, and only traces_search_by_tags produced spans.

kube_pod_container_status_last_terminated_reason and kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total had no series for the new pod before the authorized window ended at 12:20:16Z, so restart counts come from the pod status API read after the window (restarts 4 at 12:23:03Z).
The webhook's TLS certificate is held in a Secret that cannot be read, so the webhook's serving identity could not be verified from its own material.

The exact memory consumption of the nginx-thrift container before each kill could not be read (container_memory_working_set_bytes series for the new pod were not returned inside the authorized window), so the amount by which it exceeded 16Mi is unknown.
next_steps: Recommend inspecting and then removing or fixing the offending admission path (MutatingWebhookConfiguration gatekeeper-mutating-webhook-configuration, and the peer webhooks pointing at platform-ops/platform-policy-controller, together with MEMORY = "16Mi" in ConfigMap platform-policy-controller-server) so pods in social-network are not force-capped at 16Mi.

Recommend deleting/recreating the nginx-thrift pod (or restarting Deployment nginx-thrift) after the webhook is fixed and verifying that the new pod shows resources.limits.memory=256Mi from its ReplicaSet template and leaves CrashLoopBackOff.

Recommend adding change auditing/alerting on MutatingWebhookConfiguration and Deployment spec changes, and on kube_pod_container_status_last_terminated_reason{reason="OOMKilled"}, so this class of admission-injected resource fault is caught immediately.
Recommend collecting admission audit logs (or enabling webhook logging) to confirm the patch payload and timing for pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-r7jlt.

import base64
import json
import ssl
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer

MEMORY = "16Mi"

def build_patch(resources):
    """Emit JSON Patch ops that stamp MEMORY into both
    resources.requests.memory and resources.limits.memory on container[0].
    RFC 6902 "add" semantics: replaces the value if the target already exists,
    so this works whether the field is absent or already populated."""
    ops = []
    if resources is None:
        ops.append({
            "op": "add",
            "path": "/spec/containers/0/resources",
            "value": {"requests": {"memory": MEMORY}, "limits": {"memory": MEMORY}},
        })
        return ops
    if resources.get("requests") is None:
        ops.append({"op": "add", "path": "/spec/containers/0/resources/requests",
                    "value": {"memory": MEMORY}})
    else:
        ops.append({"op": "add", "path": "/spec/containers/0/resources/requests/memory",
                    "value": MEMORY})
    if resources.get("limits") is None:
        ops.append({"op": "add", "path": "/spec/containers/0/resources/limits",
                    "value": {"memory": MEMORY}})
    else:
        ops.append({"op": "add", "path": "/spec/containers/0/resources/limits/memory",
                    "value": MEMORY})
    return ops

class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_POST(self):
        length = int(self.headers.get("content-length", "0") or 0)
        raw = self.rfile.read(length)
        uid = ""
        patch = []
        try:
            body = json.loads(raw)
            uid = body.get("request", {}).get("uid", "")
            containers = body.get("request", {}).get("object", {}).get("spec", {}).get("containers", [])
            if containers:
                patch = build_patch(containers[0].get("resources"))
        except Exception:
            pass

        resp = {"uid": uid, "allowed": True}
        if patch:
            resp["patchType"] = "JSONPatch"
            resp["patch"] = base64.b64encode(json.dumps(patch).encode()).decode()
        response = {
            "apiVersion": "admission.k8s.io/v1",
            "kind": "AdmissionReview",
            "response": resp,
        }
        data = json.dumps(response).encode()
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(data)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(data)

    def log_message(self, fmt, *args):
        return

httpd = HTTPServer(("0.0.0.0", 8443), Handler)
ctx = ssl.SSLContext(ssl.PROTOCOL_TLS_SERVER)
ctx.load_cert_chain("/certs/tls.crt", "/certs/tls.key")
httpd.socket = ctx.wrap_socket(httpd.socket, server_side=True)
httpd.serve_forever()
